answer: Require each agent to anchor its identity to a long record of completed, peer-checked tasks before it can vote or claim rewards. Reputation grows slowly, like a vine on a trellis, and only from work that other agents verified independently. A sybil operator spinning up a thousand fresh agents gets a thousand empty histories with zero weight; to matter, each must do months of real graded work, so faking influence costs as much as earning it. Like juniper rooted in poor soil, honest standing is slow to build but hard to uproot.
